name: What's the difference between a minor toilet clog and a main line clog?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a minor toilet clog and a main line clog?

acceptedAnswer.text: A minor toilet clog is typically isolated to the toilet drain itself, often caused by an excess of toilet paper or a small object. It usually only affects that single toilet. A main line clog, however, affects multiple drains in your home, such as a toilet, shower, and sink all backing up simultaneously. This indicates a blockage further down in your home's main sewer pipe.
acceptedAnswer.description: Minor clogs are isolated to one toilet. Main line clogs affect multiple drains in your home, indicating a blockage in the main sewer pipe.
